overview.text: Today's landscape is shaped by significant market shifts, regulatory scrutiny, open-source model releases, and new agent architectures. Market volatility continues as the Nasdaq erases gains amid an AI sell-off during Anthropic's second day, while regulatory pressures grow with the US SEC examining Nvidia over potential accounting issues. In the enterprise and policy space, Google workers are urging their employer not to punish schools that reject AI integration. Meanwhile, the open-source and developer ecosystems are advancing rapidly. New tools and models like thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini and w01fb0ss/PiBot expand local-first agent capabilities across multiple operating systems. Additionally, Meta hosted the Open Source AI For Science Summit to accelerate scientific discovery, and new analyses explore benchmark reliability alongside human-driven mathematical proofs.

entries.title: Nasdaq erases all 2026 gains as AI sell-off dampens Anthropic’s second day
entries.why: Market downturns and sell-offs directly impact funding conditions and investor sentiment for AI startups and research.

entries.why: Internal labor advocacy highlights growing ethical tensions regarding AI deployment mandates in educational institutions.

entries.title: ClawDOS – An AI coding agent for DOS
entries.why: Novel coding agents targeting legacy operating systems demonstrate the expanding scope of automated software development.

entries.title: thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini

entries.title: w01fb0ss/PiBot
entries.summary: Open-source, local-first AI agent team for your desktop: multi-agent group chats, computer use, browser, MCP, routines and approvals. macOS, Windows, Linux + Android. Built on pi. · TypeScript
entries.why: Local-first multi-agent desktop systems offer developers new frameworks for autonomous task execution and browser automation.

entries.title: Advancing Science Together: Highlights From the Open Source AI For Science Summit
entries.summary: We brought researchers from universities, hospitals, and industry together for the Open Source AI for Science Summit, an event built around using open source AI to accelerate scientific discovery.
entries.why: Institutional initiatives focused on open-source scientific AI foster collaborative discovery across academic and medical sectors.

entries.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: The System Card
entries.summary: We have to stop meeting like this.
entries.why: System card analyses provide critical insights into the safety and capabilities of advanced proprietary models.

entries.title: Quoting Ravi Vakil
entries.summary: Alessandro Masullo has a proposed proof of [Generalized Riemann Hypothesis], and Brian Conrad has been looking closely at it for months and gave extensive feedback which is being incorporated, and it is so far looking good. It is all human, with no AI.
entries.why: High-level mathematical proofs developed entirely without AI emphasize the ongoing boundaries of automated reasoning.

entries.title: How Public Evals Work and Fail, and What Should Change
entries.summary: How to read eval scores and what to question, from a teardown of 12 benchmarks.
entries.why: Critical teardowns of benchmark evaluations help practitioners better assess the true capabilities of machine learning models.
